findings.description: After Action.SelectLightTheme, which taps lightThemeView, the test reads darkThemeView and expects "1". GenericImageOption exposes accessibilityValue "1" only for the selected option, and ThemeSelectionView selects exactly one of automatic/light/dark, so darkThemeView is "0" after light is chosen and XCTAssertEqual fails. The assertion must read lightThemeView.
findings.failureMode: wrong test result on the light-theme path
findings.title: Light theme assertion reads dark button

findings.description: POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite is guarded with @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER"). RolesGuard treats that as a minimum role, so any accepted member passes and TeamService.createInvite writes a reusable verification token that inviteMemberByToken accepts. The sibling org invite endpoint and the existing tRPC invite path require TEAM_ADMIN / OWNER|ADMIN. Change this decorator to @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN").
findings.title: Team members can mint shareable invite links

findings.description: createInvite now returns newToken.identifier (`invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`) instead of the random secret stored in verificationToken.token. Signup and team join look up verificationToken.token, so sharing the returned token or the URL built from it fails with Invalid Token / Invite not found. Return the created secret token, matching the existing options.token branch.
findings.title: Invite response returns identifier, not secret token

findings.description: buildInviteLink inverted the org check. A regular team (parentId null, isOrganization false) now gets the signup/getting-started URL, while an organization or org sub-team gets `/teams?token=...`. That is the opposite of the previous behavior and of the stated contract, so both mainline invite contexts produce the wrong destination. Restore `if (!isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink`.
findings.title: Invite links swapped for team vs org context

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn types availability.days as string[], but Prisma Availability.days is Int[] and the list API returns those integers unchanged. getScheduleListItemData, which consumes useAtomGetAllSchedules data, requires days: number[]. A real weekday list such as [1, 2, 3] is therefore not assignable to the hook result, and code that treats each day as a string gets the wrong weekday. Change days to number[] so it matches the API and the existing transformer.
findings.title: Availability days typed as strings

findings.description: The relocated Slot type changes userIds from number[] to string[]. Slot generation and the slots API still produce numeric host ids (userIds?: number[]), and onTimeslotsLoaded is typed as Record<string, Slot[]>. A consumer that receives a dynamic-event slot with userIds [12, 34] is told those ids are strings, so numeric comparisons and API calls that expect user ids fail. Restore userIds?: number[].
findings.title: Slot userIds typed as strings

findings.description: GetAvailableSlotsResponse.SlotInfo types fromUser.id as string, but IFromUser.id is number and the slots payload copies that object through. A consumer of useAvailableSlots that treats fromUser.id as a string mis-handles the numeric host id returned for out-of-office slots. Change fromUser.id to number.
findings.title: SlotInfo fromUser id typed as string

findings.description: prepare_tools now installs linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh only when the destination already exists. On a clean tools cache the file is absent, so the inverted `if gtk.exists()` skips include_bytes and write_and_make_executable entirely. The later linuxdeploy invocation always passes `--plugin gtk` and looks up `$PATH/linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh` (and the tools directory). Without that script the AppImage bundle fails instead of using the inlined plugin the change is supposed to install. The gstreamer branch in the same function still correctly uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: wrong result on the AppImage bundling path: the required linuxdeploy GTK plugin is not written, so linuxdeploy cannot load it
findings.title: GTK plugin is never installed

findings.description: write_and_make_executable used to fs::write the bytes and then chmod 0o770. The new order calls fs::set_permissions first. Every caller (AppRun, linuxdeploy, the GTK and GStreamer plugins, and the optional AppImage plugin) invokes it only when the destination does not exist, so set_permissions returns io::ErrorKind::NotFound, mapped to FileWriteError::Permissions, and the write never happens. Because FileWriteError has no From into crate::Error, the `?` in prepare_tools also fails to compile. Restore write-then-chmod so a missing file is created and then made executable.
findings.failureMode: AppImage tool download/install fails with NotFound because set_permissions runs on a path that does not exist yet
findings.title: Executable write sets permissions before creating the file

findings.description: TabProviderProtocol.onLoadingStateChanged was changed to (@MainActor @Sendable () -> Void), but Tab.onWebViewLoadingStateChanged remains (@MainActor () -> Void). TabProviderAdapter's getter returns that non-Sendable function as Sendable, and its setter assigns a Sendable closure into the non-Sendable Tab property. The Client target now builds with SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete and SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0, so this conversion is an error: toolbar loading-state observation no longer compiles. Remove @Sendable from the protocol and mock, or change Tab's stored callback and every assignment to be Sendable.
findings.title: Loading callback now requires Sendable

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction instead of .readerMode. Toolbar taps and the summarizer long-press still dispatch GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, and BrowserViewController maps .readerMode to toggleReaderMode() while mapping .readerModeLongPressAction to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(). Tapping the reader-mode button therefore opens the long-press action sheet and never toggles reader mode.
findings.failureMode: wrong result on a mainline path
findings.title: Reader-mode tap shows long-press menu

findings.description: cancelEditMode now keeps a reader-mode tab URL because the filter changed from `isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL` to `isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL`. A reader-mode page is an http localhost URL, so both checks pass and the URL is forwarded in ToolbarAction.cancelEdit. AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction then stores that URL and treats the bar as a non-empty page, so leaving edit mode from the tabs or menu button while reader mode is open shows the internal reader-mode URL instead of clearing the address bar.
findings.failureMode: wrong result on a mainline path
findings.title: Cancel edit keeps reader-mode URL

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry now reports false when readerModeState is .available and true for every other state. The metric's enabled extra records whether reader mode was opened or closed, and the previous code treated .available as about to be enabled. A tap while reader mode is available therefore records enabled=false, and a tap while it is already active records enabled=true.
findings.failureMode: wrong telemetry result on a mainline path
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry flag inverted

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn types each availability row's days as string[], but Prisma Availability.days and the schedules/all payload are Int[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper maps that response into getScheduleListItemData, whose Schedule contract requires days: number[]. Under the package strict tsconfig, a weekday array such as [1, 2, 3] is not assignable to string[], so the schedule list no longer type-checks. Restore days as number[].
findings.title: Schedule availability days typed as strings

findings.description: tsconfig.app.json changes strict from true to false. This is the project referenced by the required validate:types command, tsc -b --noEmit, so the validation pipeline no longer enforces strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes, or the other strict checks across ui-v2/src. The mandate requires strict mode to stay enabled; restore "strict": true.
findings.failureMode: security/type-checking regression in the validation pipeline
findings.title: App TypeScript strict checking disabled

findings.description: The new early return in OnboardingTests.tearDown exits the method before app.terminate() and try await super.tearDown(). On iOS 17+ this fires for every iPad test in the class (the iPad() branch is not limited to the toolbar card) and for testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone. The previous teardown always terminated the app and called super. A following test can start while the previous Firefox instance is still running, so launch/setUp races or inherits leftover UI and profile state. Replace return with a skip of only switchThemeToDarkOrLight, then always terminate and call super.
findings.failureMode: On iOS 17+, every iPad OnboardingTests case and testSelectBottomPlacement returns from tearDown before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(), leaving the app running and skipping XCTest teardown.
findings.title: tearDown return skips app termination

findings.description: testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders was renamed to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders. XCTest only discovers instance methods whose names start with test, so this case is no longer invoked by class-wide runs (Smoketest, TAESmokeTestPlan, ExperimentIntegrationTests, and others list ShareLongPressTests as a class). AccessibilityTestPlan still skips the old identifier ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders(), which does not match the new name. The bookmarks-to-Reminders share path is therefore untested. Restore the test prefix.
findings.failureMode: Renaming the method off the test prefix removes it from XCTest discovery, so the bookmarks Reminders case is never executed.
findings.title: Reminders test method no longer runs

findings.description: The textarea is controlled by events.join("\n") while onChange writes e.target.value.split("\n") unchanged. Pressing Enter stores a trailing "", and the next render joins it away, so the caret jumps and the new line cannot be typed: "prefect.flow-run.Completed" then Enter then "prefect.flow-run.Failed" never becomes a two-event array. Clearing the field or leaving a trailing newline also stores [""] or ["event", ""]; an empty pattern matches nothing, so the saved trigger does not fire for the events entered. Keep the raw textarea text until blur or submission, then trim and drop blank lines before field.onChange.
findings.failureMode: wrong form value: newline-separated custom events are dropped or saved with empty patterns
findings.title: Custom event textarea drops lines while typing

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields always binds the selected status to trigger.expect, including when posture is Proactive. The established trigger contract and DeploymentStatusTriggerFields store the state being stayed in on trigger.after and leave expect empty so a proactive trigger fires on the absence of any following event. Selecting Paused and Stays in therefore submits after=[] and expect=["prefect.work-pool.paused"], which waits for that event to be absent instead of starting after it and never fires a "stayed in Paused" automation. Bind the status field to trigger.after when posture is Proactive, matching DeploymentStatusTriggerFields.
findings.failureMode: wrong trigger payload: proactive work-pool status is stored as an expected event rather than the after event
findings.title: Work pool proactive status writes expect, not after

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields always binds the selected status to trigger.expect, including when posture is Proactive. The established trigger contract and DeploymentStatusTriggerFields store the state being stayed in on trigger.after and leave expect empty so a proactive trigger fires on the absence of any following event. Selecting Paused and Stays in therefore submits after=[] and expect=["prefect.work-queue.paused"], which waits for that event to be absent instead of starting after it and never fires a "stayed in Paused" automation. Bind the status field to trigger.after when posture is Proactive, matching DeploymentStatusTriggerFields.
findings.failureMode: wrong trigger payload: proactive work-queue status is stored as an expected event rather than the after event
findings.title: Work queue proactive status writes expect, not after

findings.description: CustomTriggerFields always writes the entered events to trigger.expect, even after the user selects the Proactive ("Stays in") posture. DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields move that value to trigger.after for Proactive so the trigger starts after those events and fires when no subsequent event arrives. A custom proactive trigger therefore submits after=[] and expect=[entered events], so the automation waits for those events not to happen instead of staying in them, and never fires the requested proactive automation. When posture is Proactive, write the textarea values to trigger.after.
findings.failureMode: wrong trigger payload: custom proactive events are stored as expected events rather than after events
findings.title: Custom proactive events write expect, not after

findings.description: statusFieldName switches the status FormField between trigger.expect and trigger.after when posture changes, but nothing copies or clears the previously written array. Select Ready while Reactive, then switch to Proactive: the select reads the empty trigger.after and shows the placeholder, while trigger.expect remains ["prefect.deployment.ready"]. Submitting in that state sends a proactive trigger with an empty after list, so the automation does not start after the chosen status and never fires for "stayed in Ready". On posture change, move the selected status onto the newly active field and clear the inactive one.
findings.failureMode: wrong trigger payload: selected deployment status remains on the inactive expect/after field after posture changes
findings.title: Posture switch leaves deployment status on the wrong field

findings.description: tsconfig.app.json flips compilerOptions.strict from true to false. ui-v2's validate:types and build scripts run tsc -b, which uses this project config, so the required strict type check no longer runs for ui-v2/src. Type errors that strict mode would have failed the build on now pass validation.
findings.failureMode: validation bypass: tsc -b no longer enforces strict checks on ui-v2/src
findings.title: App TypeScript strict checking disabled

findings.description: The work-pool threshold input writes parseInt(e.target.value), unlike the sibling trigger fields which use Number. Clearing the input makes e.target.value "" and parseInt("") is NaN, so trigger.threshold becomes NaN. EventTriggerSchema requires a number of at least 1, and NaN fails that check, so the wizard's Next validation rejects the step and the input shows blank rather than the cleared numeric state the other fields produce. Use Number, as the other threshold inputs do, or reject the empty value before calling onChange.
findings.failureMode: validation failure: clearing the work-pool threshold stores NaN and the trigger step cannot validate
findings.title: Work pool threshold parseInt yields NaN

findings.description: get_internal now reads original_identifier from config["bundle"] as a string. The Tauri identifier is a top-level string, and bundle is an object, so this is always None. write_options and read_options then fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier" (or look up a nonexistent server-addr file) for every mobile build that has a valid identifier. Restore config.get("identifier").
findings.title: Original identifier read from bundle object

findings.description: The JSON/JSON5 schema gate was changed from || to &&. Path::extension() cannot be both "json" and "json5", so config_schema_validator().iter_errors is never reached. Invalid tauri.conf.json and tauri.conf.json5 files that previously exited with logged schema errors now pass CLI validation. Restore the || condition.
findings.title: Schema validation condition is unreachable

findings.description: merge_with still merges CLI patches into a local JSON value, but the assignment back to config_metadata.inner was removed. Only the --config extension map and TAURI_CONFIG env var are updated, so later readers of the loaded Config (dev_url, bundle settings, plugins) keep the pre-merge values. Android/iOS studio scripts call merge_with after reload and then read that handle, so --config overrides are silently dropped. Restore config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies merged config

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops with `j <= keys_result->numkeys`, one past the last valid key. On any command with keys (cluster enabled), the extra iteration reads keys[numkeys].pos and argv at that index, then writes slot_buffer[numkeys] past the malloc of numkeys ints. That is an out-of-bounds read/write on the main command path (preprocessCommand via extractKeysAndSlot, and getSlotFromCommand for ASM propagation) and can crash or corrupt the heap before the slot is returned. The base loop used `j < numkeys`. Fix the bound to `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: out-of-bounds read crashes slot extraction on every keyed command
findings.title: Slot extraction reads one past the key list

findings.description: The new slot_buffer is allocated with malloc and released with free, which violates the zmalloc/zfree rule and bypasses Redis memory accounting on every keyed command. The buffer is only written, never read, so it does not affect the slot result. malloc failure is also unchecked, so a NULL return is immediately written at slot_buffer[j]. Remove the buffer entirely (the first_slot comparison already detects cross-slot); if a buffer is required, allocate it with zmalloc and free it with zfree.
findings.failureMode: allocator-rule violation and untracked allocation on every keyed command; NULL malloc is not checked before write
findings.title: Slot buffer uses malloc/free and is never read

findings.description: prepare_tools now writes linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh only when the file already exists (`if gtk.exists()`), inverting the previous `if !gtk.exists()` guard. On a clean tools cache the inlined script is never copied, so linuxdeploy is invoked with `--plugin gtk` against a missing plugin and AppImage bundling fails. Restore the negation so the script is written when absent.
findings.title: GTK plugin is never written on a fresh cache

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write. The first install of AppRun, linuxdeploy, the gstreamer plugin, or the appimage plugin creates a path that does not exist yet, so set_permissions returns NotFound and the `?` in prepare_tools aborts bundling before any bytes are written. Write the file first, then set mode 0o770, as the previous function did.
findings.title: chmod runs before the tool file exists

findings.description: On i686, tools_arch is the target triple prefix "i686", and linuxdeploy_arch rewrites that to "i383" only for the local filename. The download URL previously used linuxdeploy_arch and now interpolates raw arch, requesting linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage. The published linuxdeploy release assets are linuxdeploy-i386.AppImage (plus aarch64, armhf, and x86_64), so neither i686 nor i383 exists. A 32-bit AppImage bundle therefore 404s on the first linuxdeploy download and prepare_tools returns an error instead of installing the tool. Point the URL at the published i386 asset (and keep the cached filename consistent with that download).
findings.title: i686 linuxdeploy URL does not match published assets

findings.description: members-api.js now requires ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link, but the only file in that directory is still MagicLink.js. Node module resolution is case-sensitive in production, so initializing MembersAPI throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before magic-link sign-in can be constructed. Point the require back at MagicLink until that file is actually renamed.
findings.title: Members API requires missing magic-link module

findings.description: email-analytics-service-wrapper.js now requires ../email-service/email-event-storage and ../email-service/email-event-processor, but those files remain EmailEventStorage.js and EmailEventProcessor.js. When email analytics initializes, Node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and event storage is never constructed. Keep the PascalCase requires until those files are renamed.
findings.title: Email analytics requires unrenamed event modules

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from require('express'). Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after express require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from require('body-parser'). Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after body-parser require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from require('@tryghost/errors'). Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after errors require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from require('@tryghost/logging'). Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after logging require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from the payments-service require. Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after payments-service require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from the token-service require. Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after token-service require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from the geolocation-service require. Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after geolocation-service require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from the member-bread-service require. Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after member-bread-service require

findings.description: The rename dropped the trailing semicolon from the member-repository require. Rule 19 requires an explicit semicolon, so this statement now depends on ASI. Restore the semicolon.
findings.title: Missing semicolon after member-repository require

findings.description: get_internal now reads original_identifier from the top-level "bundle" object and then treats that object as a string. Config.identifier lives at the root, and "bundle" is an object, so as_str() is always None. original_identifier() therefore returns None for every valid tauri.conf.json. write_options and read_options then fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier" instead of writing or reading the mobile CLI options socket address file, so Android Studio and Xcode builds cannot recover the CLI options. Restore config.get("identifier").
findings.title: Bundle key never yields original identifier

findings.description: The json/json5 schema gate was changed from || to &&. Path::extension() cannot be both "json" and "json5", so config_schema_validator().iter_errors is never reached and exit(1) on invalid JSON/JSON5 config never runs. A tauri.conf.json that fails the bundled schema (unknown fields, wrong types, missing required identifier) is now accepted by the CLI instead of being rejected before build/dev. Restore the original OR so either extension is validated.
findings.title: Schema validation condition is unreachable

findings.description: merge_with still serializes the loaded config, merges the CLI patches into a local value, and sets TAURI_CONFIG, but the assignment of that merged value back to config_metadata.inner was replaced with an extensions-map insert. Callers such as the Android Studio and Xcode scripts then read the pre-merge config, so --config overrides passed through those scripts (devUrl, identifier, plugin settings) are ignored and the built app uses the unpatched tauri.conf.json. Reassign config_metadata.inner from the merged value; keep the extensions insert only as additional bookkeeping.
findings.title: merge_with no longer applies merged config

findings.description: config_schema_validator builds the schema parse and expect on one 156-character line. Project rustfmt max_width is 100, so cargo fmt --all -- --check fails on this new line. Wrap the include_str/expect call so it fits the configured width.
findings.title: Schema parse line exceeds rustfmt width

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the toolbar's leading and trailing anchors are both constrained to rightSkeletonAddressBar. The previous leading constraint used leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor. Both skeleton bars are placed outside the container (left trailing to the container leading edge, right leading from the container trailing edge), so the toolbar is now required to sit in the gap to the right of the right skeleton instead of between the two skeletons. The address bar is laid out off-screen or unsatisfiable when swiping tabs is enabled. Restore the leading constraint to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.title: Swipe toolbar pinned to the wrong skeleton

findings.description: updateToolbarLayout was supposed to fade in trailing page-action buttons after the pageActionStack rename, but the fourth array element is now browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews, which is already the first element. updateActionStack sets alpha to 0 for newly added buttons, then this animation is the only place that sets those buttons' alpha to 1. With animated true and reduce-motion off, reload/share and other trailing page actions stay invisible. Use trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.title: Trailing page actions never fade in

findings.description: updateActionSpacing now decides the location divider width from leadingPageActionStack instead of the renamed trailing page-action stack. The divider sits between the URL field and trailing page actions, and configureUX sets its width from browserActionsAddressBarDividerWidth before this function overwrites it. When trailing actions exist and leading ones do not, the constant is forced to 0, so the divider is missing. Check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.title: Address divider ignores trailing page actions

findings.description: `make check` runs `ruff check ./api`, and ruff reports SIM300 at this new assertion because the constant is on the left. The comparison is not inverted, but the selected SIM rules fail the check until it is rewritten as `result.outputs["output"] == "1, two, 3.0, True"`.
findings.failureMode: The required ruff check command fails on the new assertion, so the registered lint gate does not pass.
findings.title: Ruff check fails on Yoda assertion

findings.description: `ruff format --check` fails on this file because the new `test_run_with_string_concatenation` signature is split across lines 662-664 even though it fits in 120 characters. Collapse it to one line, which is the rewrite `ruff format` applies.
findings.failureMode: The required ruff format gate rewrites this new signature, so `make format` / `make lint` does not pass as committed.
findings.title: Ruff format fails on split signature

findings.description: `ruff format --check` also rewrites the new `test_run_with_conditional_if_else` signature at lines 703-705 into a single line. This is a separate site from the concatenation signature: fixing only line 662 leaves this function unformatted and `make format` still fails.
findings.failureMode: The required ruff format gate rewrites this second new signature, so the file still fails format after the first signature is fixed.
findings.title: Ruff format fails on second split signature

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops `j <= keys_result->numkeys` and then reads `keys_result->keys[j]` and writes `slot_buffer[j]`. The buffer is only `numkeys` ints and the key array has only `numkeys` entries (base used `j < numkeys`). On every clustered command with at least one key — GET, SET, MGET — the last iteration is an out-of-bounds read of the key position and an out-of-bounds write. That is a reachable crash or a garbage slot decision on the main command path. Change the bound to `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Off-by-one loop indexes keys_result->keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys], both out of bounds. Any clustered command with keys crashes or reads a garbage key before slot routing.
findings.title: Slot extraction reads one past the key list

findings.description: The new temporary slot buffer is allocated with malloc and released with free. AGENTS.md requires src/ dynamic allocations to use zmalloc/zcalloc/zrealloc and zfree; a direct malloc/free outside zmalloc itself fails that rule and is invisible to Redis used-memory tracking. The buffer is never read after it is filled, so the allocation does not contribute to the returned slot. Remove the buffer, or if it is kept, allocate it with zmalloc and free it with zfree.
findings.failureMode: Direct malloc/free bypasses Redis memory accounting and violates the zmalloc mandate. The buffer is also unused for the result, so the allocation is dead.
findings.title: Slot buffer uses malloc/free instead of zmalloc

findings.description: POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite is decorated with @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER"). RolesGuard treats the listed role as a minimum, and TEAM_ROLES orders MEMBER below ADMIN, so any accepted member is authorized. The PR contract, the sibling OrganizationsTeamsInviteController, and the web createInvite permission check all require admin/owner. A member can therefore mint a token that inviteMemberByToken accepts as a join credential for that team. Change the decorator to TEAM_ADMIN.
findings.failureMode: A regular TEAM_MEMBER passes RolesGuard.hasMinimumRole and can mint a reusable team join token.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows any team member

findings.description: The new create path returns token: newToken.identifier. identifier is the stored lookup key invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}, while the secret written to verificationToken.token is the random hex. inviteLink is still built with that hex, so data.token is not contained in inviteLink and callers that redeem data.token fail: inviteMemberByToken looks up verificationToken.token, and signup looks up the unique token. The options.token branch still returns existingToken.token, so only newly created invites are wrong. Return newToken.token (the local token variable).
findings.failureMode: New invite responses return the lookup identifier as token, so the shared link cannot be redeemed.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of token

findings.description: buildInviteLink previously returned `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=` when isOrgContext was false and the signup/getting-started URL when it was true. The condition is now `if (isOrgContext) return teamInviteLink`, which swaps those destinations. createInvite still passes isOrganizationOrATeamInOrganization, so a regular team (parentId null, isOrganization false) gets the org signup URL, while an organization or org sub-team gets `/teams`. The existing-token branch uses the same helper, so every caller, including the web createInvite mutation and OrganizationsTeamsInviteController, emits the wrong link. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)`.
findings.failureMode: Regular teams get signup links and organization teams get /teams links, so invitees land on the wrong join flow.
findings.title: Invite link context is inverted

findings.description: Email analytics init now requires ../email-service/email-event-storage, but that file was not renamed and still exists only as EmailEventStorage.js. Calling init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and never constructs the analytics service. Restore the require to ../email-service/EmailEventStorage.
findings.title: Email analytics requires missing storage module

findings.description: Email analytics init now requires ../email-service/email-event-processor, but that file was not renamed and still exists only as EmailEventProcessor.js. Calling init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the processor can be constructed. Restore the require to ../email-service/EmailEventProcessor.
findings.title: Email analytics requires missing processor module

findings.description: The members API require was changed to ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link, but MagicLink.js was not renamed. Loading members-api.js throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and members sign-in cannot start. Restore the require to ../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink.
findings.title: Members API requires missing magic-link module

findings.description: Workflow run inputs and outputs are stored with json.dumps, which emits non-ASCII as \\uXXXX. The previous keyword pattern encoded the term with unicode_escape and rewrote \\u to \\\\u so ILIKE matched that stored form. The new code only runs escape_like_pattern on the raw keyword, so a search for a CJK or other non-ASCII term (for example 测试) looks for the literal characters and misses runs whose JSON contains \\u6d4b\\u8bd5. Restore the unicode_escape transform on the keyword used against WorkflowRun.inputs and WorkflowRun.outputs before applying LIKE escaping.
findings.title: Workflow keyword search no longer matches JSON unicode escapes

findings.description: escape_like_pattern prefixes %, _, and \ with a backslash, but the IRIS fallback binds that pattern with ESCAPE '|'. A query containing % or _ (for example "50%") becomes LIKE '%50\%%' ESCAPE '|', so IRIS treats % as a wildcard and backslash as a literal. Full-text fallback then matches unrelated chunks and fails to find text that actually contains a backslash. Use ESCAPE '\' (or escape with '|' inside the helper) so the escape character matches the inserted prefixes.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE escape character does not match helper

findings.description: escape_like_pattern inserts a single backslash before %, _, and \, but the interpolated SQL uses ESCAPE '\\\\', which sets the escape character to two backslashes. A query such as "50%" therefore becomes LIKE '%50\\%%' ESCAPE '\\' (two-backslash escape). ClickZetta does not treat the single backslash as the escape, so % and _ stay wildcards and a literal backslash in the query is not matched. The clause must be ESCAPE '\\' so it agrees with the one-backslash prefixes the helper emits.
findings.title: ClickZetta LIKE escape string does not match helper

findings.description: "not contains" escapes the value with backslash prefixes but calls json_field.notlike without escape="\\", unlike contains/start with/end with. For a metadata value such as "50%", the predicate is NOT LIKE '%50\\%%' with the default escape, so the backslash is literal and % remains a wildcard. Documents that do not contain the literal "50%" are excluded, and the negation matches almost everything. Pass escape="\\" to notlike, the same way the other three branches do.
findings.title: not contains filter omits LIKE escape clause

findings.description: hincrbyfloatCommand now calls hashTypeSet with only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE, dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL that the previous code passed. hashTypeSet treats a missing KEEP_TTL flag as "remove the field's expiry": listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) for listpackex and hfieldPersist for hashtable. That write happens on the primary before rewriteClientCommandVector, so HINCRBYFLOAT on a field that already has a TTL (HSETEX/HEXPIRE) clears that TTL on the master itself. The rewritten HSETEX KEEPTTL only preserves whatever TTL remains, so replicas and AOF replay also end up with no expiry. The new test only checks replica HTTL against the master after the increment, so both sides agreeing on a cleared TTL still passes. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this hashTypeSet call.
findings.failureMode: wrong result on the mainline write path: field expiration is removed on the primary before replication
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT clears field TTL on the master

findings.description: This diff removes static from addHashFieldToReply. Every call remains inside src/t_hash.c (hgetCommand, hmgetCommand, and the HGETDEL/HGETEX paths); there is no declaration in server.h and no caller in any other compilation unit. AGENTS.md rule 7 requires functions used only within a single source file to be declared static. Restore static on this definition. The replacement may exist outside the visible diff, but nothing visible re-establishes the internal linkage.
findings.failureMode: internal helper is exported, violating the repository static-function mandate and polluting the link symbol table
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply is no longer static

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the toolbar's leading edge is now pinned to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor while its trailing edge remains pinned to that same view's leadingAnchor. The right skeleton begins at the container's trailing edge and is nearly the container width, so these required constraints cannot be satisfied and the toolbar collapses or logs an Auto Layout conflict. Pin the leading edge to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor.
findings.title: Swiping toolbar constraints conflict

findings.description: updateToolbarLayout now appends browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews twice and omits trailingPageActionStack. New trailing page buttons are initialized to alpha 0, so reload, reader-mode, and other trailing actions remain invisible after both animated and non-animated toolbar updates. Restore trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews in the animation list.
findings.title: Trailing page actions never fade in

findings.description: updateActionSpacing now enables the location divider only when leadingPageActionStack is non-empty. The divider sits between the URL field and trailingPageActionStack, and configureUX sets its width before updateActions calls updateActionSpacing, so the latter wins. A normal loading page has only trailing actions such as stop/reload and empty leading actions, collapsing the default 4-point divider; leading-only actions incorrectly reserve its width. Check trailingPageActionStack instead.
findings.title: Address divider follows the wrong action stack

findings.description: The display name was changed to Xcode 16.4.0, but the script still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` on both the public (line 167 display, path on 166) and internal (line 393 display, path on 392) macOS-15 jobs. macOS-15 images do not contain Xcode 15.2, so xcode-select fails and the macOS build never starts. Point both scripts at the Xcode 16.4 developer directory that the display name claims to select.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI step exits non-zero before the build because the selected Xcode.app path does not exist on the macOS-15 image
findings.title: macOS job selects missing Xcode 15.2

findings.description: The internal macOS job display name was changed to Xcode 16.4.0, but the script on the preceding line still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` after the pool was switched to macOS-15. That image does not contain Xcode 15.2, so the step fails and the internal macOS build never starts. Select `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.app/Contents/Developer` (or the image's actual 16.4 path).
findings.failureMode: internal macOS CI step exits non-zero before the build because the selected Xcode.app path does not exist on the macOS-15 image
findings.title: Internal macOS job selects missing Xcode 15.2

findings.description: PreReleaseVersionLabel is now `servicing`, but PreReleaseBrandingLabel is only assigned for alpha, preview, rc, and rtm. Directory.Build.targets always interpolates `$(PreReleaseBrandingLabel) Build $(VersionSuffix)` into non-stabilized package branding, so servicing builds produce a leading-space branding string such as ` Build <suffix>` instead of a servicing label. Add a condition that sets PreReleaseBrandingLabel when PreReleaseVersionLabel is servicing.
findings.failureMode: non-stabilized servicing package branding is computed with an empty PreReleaseBrandingLabel and a leading space
findings.title: Servicing builds lose branding label

findings.description: The BUILD002 error that blocks removed package references in servicing builds is now also gated on `$(AspNetCorePatchVersion) == '1'`. IsServicingBuild stays true for every later 10.0.x patch, so once the patch version is incremented past 1, a servicing project that drops a baseline reference no longer fails the build. The error text still says such a change is not allowed in a servicing update. Remove the patch-version clause so the existing servicing guard applies to every patch.
findings.failureMode: servicing builds after 10.0.1 silently accept removed baseline package references that BUILD002 is documented to reject
findings.title: BUILD002 skipped after patch 1

findings.description: search_by_full_text now prefixes LIKE metacharacters with backslash via escape_like_pattern, but the SQL uses ESCAPE '|'. IRIS therefore treats '\' as a literal and '|' as the escape character. A query containing %, _, or \ (for example "50%" or "test_data") is matched as a wildcard pattern or fails to match the literal text, so the no-index fallback returns the wrong documents. Escape the pattern with '|' (and pass that character to the helper) or set ESCAPE '\' to match the helper.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE escape character does not match helper

findings.description: The "not contains" branch escapes %, _, and \ with escape_like_pattern but calls json_field.notlike without escape="\\", unlike contains, start with, and end with. SQLAlchemy 2.0.29 ColumnOperators.not_like (aliased as notlike) accepts escape and renders ESCAPE. With the default escape, a metadata value such as "50%" becomes NOT LIKE '%50\\%%', so the backslash is literal, '%' stays a wildcard, and documents that should be excluded still match (literal backslash searches miss). Pass escape="\\" on this notlike call.
findings.title: not contains LIKE escape clause omitted

findings.description: testCheckSystemThemeChanges selects Light mode via Action.SelectLightTheme, which taps AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.lightThemeView. The following assertion reads darkThemeView and expects its accessibility value to be "1". GenericImageOption sets accessibilityValue to "1" only on the selected option and "0" on the others, so after a successful light selection darkThemeView is "0" and XCTAssertEqual fails. The light-mode step of case 3298823 therefore fails even when light theme is correctly selected. Read lightThemeView instead.
findings.title: Light theme assertion reads dark theme button

findings.description: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection pushes TopSitesSettingsViewController, which has no Done button. Done is the Homepage settings right-bar item that calls settingsDelegate?.didFinish() and dismisses the entire settings stack. The reordered flow taps that Done while still on the pushed shortcuts screen, then calls navigator.goto(NewTabScreen). The navigator is still at HomeSettings and looks for its back button on a screen that is already gone, so the test times out instead of verifying that top sites were removed. Pop the shortcuts screen first (its back button is titled Shortcuts), then tap Done.
findings.title: Done dismisses settings before leaving shortcuts

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction. A toolbar reader-mode tap dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, which reaches this handler; BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions then calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() instead of toggleReaderMode(). The page is added to the reading list and reader mode is never toggled. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.title: Reader-mode tap opens reading-list sheet

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry now maps readerModeState .available to isReaderModeEnabled false and every other state to true, inverting the previous mapping and the adjacent comment that the action will enable reader mode. A tap when reader mode is available therefore records reader_mode_button_tapped with enabled=false, and a tap that disables an active reader mode records enabled=true. Restore case .available: true and default: false.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: The public macOS pool is switched to macOS-15, whose installed Xcode apps are 16.x only (default `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app`). The step display name is updated to "Use XCode 16.4.0", but the command still runs `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer`. That path does not exist on macOS-15, so xcode-select exits non-zero and every public macOS job fails before the build. The internal job has the same stale command beside its updated display name at line 393. The release/10.0 pipeline selects `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app/Contents/Developer`.
findings.failureMode: every macOS CI job fails at xcode-select
findings.title: macOS-15 job selects missing Xcode 15.2

findings.description: BUILD002 previously failed every servicing build when UnusedBaselinePackageReference was non-empty. The added `AspNetCorePatchVersion == 1` clause makes the error fire only for the first patch. Versions.props sets PreReleaseVersionLabel to servicing, so IsServicingBuild stays true when the next servicing update increments AspNetCorePatchVersion to 2 or later. A removed baseline package reference then no longer fails the build, and a servicing package can ship without a dependency its callers still require. docs/BuildErrors.md still says BUILD002 is not suppressible and applies to servicing builds generally. The current release/10.0 targets file no longer contains this patch-version exception.
findings.failureMode: servicing reference removal is no longer a build error after patch 1
findings.title: BUILD002 baseline check is disabled after patch 1

findings.description: The new comment says PreReleaseBrandingLabel is calculated from PreReleaseVersionLabel, and PreReleaseVersionLabel is now servicing. The conditions only set a label for alpha, preview, rc, and rtm, so a servicing build leaves PreReleaseBrandingLabel empty. Directory.Build.targets then builds BrandingVersionSuffix as " Build $(VersionSuffix)" whenever VersionSuffix is set. Non-stabilized servicing installers therefore display a version such as "10.0.1 Build …" instead of "10.0.1 Servicing Build …". The current release/10.0 Versions.props includes a servicing condition that sets the label to Servicing.
findings.failureMode: non-stabilized servicing installers are branded without a release label
findings.title: Servicing builds lose their branding label

findings.description: The new iPad/testSelectBottomPlacement branch returns from override tearDown() before app.terminate() and try await super.tearDown(). On every iOS 17 iPad OnboardingTests method, including tests that call switchThemeToDarkOrLight("Dark"), and on testSelectBottomPlacement, XCTest never runs BaseTestCase.tearDown(). The app therefore remains running and superclass cleanup is skipped, contaminating subsequent tests. The early return should be limited to skipping the theme reset.
findings.failureMode: On iOS 17, iPad and testSelectBottomPlacement return before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(), leaving the app process and XCTest lifecycle cleanup incomplete for later tests.
findings.title: Early teardown return skips app cleanup

findings.description: testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders was renamed to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders. XCTest does not treat methods without the test prefix as tests, so TestRail case 2864380 never runs. AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan still lists ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders(), which no longer matches any method. Restore the test prefix (and update the plan only if the name intentionally changes).
findings.failureMode: XCTest only discovers methods beginning with test, so the renamed method is never invoked and AccessibilityTestPlan still skips a selector that no longer exists.
findings.title: Renamed share test is no longer executed

findings.description: hashTypeSet in hincrbyfloatCommand is now called with only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE. On both listpack-ex and hashtable encodings, omitting HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL calls listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) or hfieldPersist and clears an existing field expiry. HINCRBY still passes HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, and the new HSETEX KEEPTTL rewrite only affects what is propagated after the local write. After HSETEX key EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 then HINCRBYFLOAT key f1 1.1, HTTL on the master returns -1 while the replica that applies HSETEX KEEPTTL keeps the TTL, so the patch inverts the original master/replica mismatch. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this call.
findings.failureMode: wrong result on the main write path: the writer's field expiration is removed while the value is updated
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT drops field TTL on the writer

findings.description: The diff drops static from addHashFieldToReply, which is only called from hgetCommand, hmgetCommand, hgetdel, and hgetex inside src/t_hash.c. Mandate 7 requires a single-file helper to stay static. Restore static; nothing in the HINCRBYFLOAT rewrite needs the symbol exported.
findings.failureMode: internal helper is exported from the translation unit, violating the static-helper mandate
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply is no longer static
